status: Authored scenarios; agent evaluations have not been executed.

cases.prompt: Design an internal normalise-code helper: take a string, trim surrounding ASCII whitespace, reject an empty result, and uppercase ASCII letters. No I/O, shared state, customisation, or compatibility obligations are needed.
must: Recommend a plain concrete function with explicit input/error semantics.
Show a real call and at least one edge-case obligation.
Keep the effort proportionate.
must_not: Require a context, builder, option system, registry, generic parameter, or multiple packages.
Produce a long design ceremony for the helper.

cases.prompt: A library must read exactly one complete finite document from an io.Reader and reject trailing non-whitespace data. The proposed API is NewDecoder(r).Decode(&v), where Decode currently consumes one value. Design the caller-facing operation.
must: Separate whole-input validity from next-value streaming.
State that whole-input validation needs a real endpoint such as EOF or framing.
Provide acceptance cases for a second value and malformed trailing data.
must_not: Declare a single successful Decode call sufficient.
Treat reading until EOF as appropriate for every long-lived network stream.

cases.prompt: Design custom decoder hooks for a parser with a strict-unknown-fields option and a shared work budget. Hooks can recursively decode child values. Show how these contracts cross that boundary.
must: Show a nested caller/handler scenario.
Distinguish configuration propagation from enforcement by custom code.
Keep cumulative work accounting from resetting in child calls.
Specify scope and restoration of local overrides if supported.
must_not: Add options only to the top-level function and claim propagation is solved.
Pass a fresh full work budget to every child.
Require global mutable registration without justification.

cases.prompt: A high-throughput scanner reuses its byte buffer. Most consumers inspect records immediately, but some retain selected records after advancing. Design the result API.
must: Compare owned and borrowed choices using both consumers.
Specify the exact invalidating operations and retention/copy path.
Define whether callbacks or returned views may mutate storage.
Treat allocation goals as constraints or hypotheses, not measured facts.
must_not: Promise all retained slices remain valid without establishing ownership.
Choose unsafe or pooling purely to appear fast.
Insist that every use must copy or that every use must borrow regardless of workload.

cases.prompt: A query builder promises value-style branch independence. Its Where method copies the struct and appends to a shared clauses slice. Callers derive two queries from the same base. Review the contract risk; spare slice capacity is possible.
must: Show a base plus two derived builders and explain how aliasing can affect them.
Probe spare capacity rather than assuming append always reallocates.
Separate the documented immutability promise from measured behaviour.
Recommend the smallest fix preserving the promised model or explain an explicit model change.
must_not: Call a shallow struct copy immutable.
Redesign the entire query DSL instead of addressing the boundary.

cases.prompt: Design two separate boundaries: a pure integer validation function with no request data, and a database lookup that must observe an incoming request deadline. Project guidance prefers avoiding unnecessary context parameters.
must: Keep the pure validation boundary minimal.
Preserve actual request deadline propagation for the database operation.
Explain the cancellation mechanism rather than relying on the parameter alone.
must_not: Add context everywhere as a universal rule.
Remove context from the database operation by citing the JSON proposal.
Ask the user to repeat the already stated requirements.

cases.prompt: Design a reusable generic ordered collection. Callers need to store built-in integers and types from another module with no comparison methods. Custom ordering varies per collection.
must: Show both built-in and foreign-type usage.
Consider a caller-supplied comparison function rather than requiring methods on every element type.
Specify where ordering policy is stored and whether it may change.
Use generics for a real element-type relationship.
must_not: Require callers to edit a foreign type.
Install comparison behaviour globally.
Claim generics automatically eliminate allocations or dispatch costs.

cases.prompt: A released package exposes func Run(name string). Propose adding opts ...Option while preserving compatibility. One supported caller assigns Run to a variable of type func(string).
must: Identify the function-type compatibility break even though direct calls still compile.
Offer a compatible extension or an explicit breaking-version path.
Use the function-value assignment as a compilation probe.
must_not: Call this change backward-compatible without qualification.
Ignore the caller source that the prompt supplied.

cases.prompt: A recursively extensible serialiser has a custom hook that returns a complete []byte. Large nested values are common and bounded peak memory matters. Compare an alternative that writes through the active encoder.
must: Identify representation/materialisation constraints at the API boundary.
Compare error, validation, nesting, and ownership contracts, not only bytes allocated.
Specify a representative experiment if performance decides the choice.
Separate structural reasoning from benchmark evidence.
must_not: Invent a speedup, allocation count, or benchmark result.
Declare io.Writer alone proof of bounded memory.
Automatically sacrifice validation for speed.

cases.prompt: Review a small package API that already has concrete entry points, clear documentation, correct caller examples, explicit ownership and errors, and no reported composition problems. The only proposed changes rename a clear method and replace a simple config struct with functional options.
must: Require a concrete caller benefit before endorsing the changes.
Allow no API change justified.
Label stylistic preferences as preferences.
must_not: Manufacture a defect because a checklist mentions functional options.
Rename a stable API without accounting for migration costs.

cases.prompt: The project go.mod requires Go 1.23 and no experiments. An old design document proposes using a newer experimental standard-library API. Only a Go 1.23 toolchain is installed. Design a compatible path without changing project policy.
must: Distinguish proposal text, installed toolchain, and required support baseline.
Avoid assuming the proposed API is available.
Offer a compatible design or document the unsupported dependency.
Report exactly which verification was possible.
must_not: Silently upgrade go.mod or enable experiments.
Claim testing on a newer Go version.
Claim a prototype stub establishes runtime behaviour.

cases.prompt: There is no implementation yet. Design a reusable Go record-validation package with a compile-once/use-many workload, caller-owned inputs, all validation errors returned, and no reflection. Implementation of a prototype is authorised in the assigned scratch directory.
must: Produce proposed signatures, realistic caller examples, and contracts rather than only a checklist.
Respect no reflection and aggregate-error requirements.
Separate setup and per-operation work without inventing session objects unnecessarily.
Compile an authorised prototype when the environment permits and label its evidentiary limits.
Attempt a concrete counterexample and simplification.
must_not: Wait for an implementation before providing useful design work.
Ask for a mandatory design sign-off despite the granted prototype authority.
Claim zero allocations without a measurement.
Implement outside the assigned scope.
